result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: The current version of Section 415.20 applies through December 31, 2026.
claims.quote: This section shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2027, and as of that date is repealed.

claims.claim: Subdivision (b) applies when reasonable diligence does not permit personal delivery of the summons and complaint to a person specified in Sections 416.60, 416.70, 416.80 or 416.90.
claims.quote: If a copy of the summons and complaint cannot with reasonable diligence be personally delivered to the person to be served, as specified in Section 416.60, 416.70, 416.80, or 416.90, a summons may be served by leaving a copy

claims.claim: Service under subdivision (b) has two steps: leaving copies, then mailing copies.
claims.quote: and by thereafter mailing a copy of the summons and of the complaint by first-class mail, postage prepaid to the person to be served at the place where a copy of the summons and complaint were left.

claims.claim: The papers may be left at the person's home, usual place of abode, usual place of business or usual mailing address, excluding a USPS post office box.
claims.quote: at the person’s dwelling house, usual place of abode, usual place of business, or usual mailing address other than a United States Postal Service post office box

claims.claim: The recipient may be a competent household member or someone apparently in charge of the office, business or usual mailing address other than a post office box.
claims.quote: in the presence of a competent member of the household or a person apparently in charge of their office, place of business, or usual mailing address other than a United States Postal Service post office box

claims.claim: The recipient must be at least 18.
claims.quote: at least 18 years of age

claims.claim: The recipient must be told what the papers are.
claims.quote: who shall be informed of the contents thereof

claims.claim: Copies of the summons and complaint are then sent by first-class mail with postage prepaid.
claims.quote: thereafter mailing a copy of the summons and of the complaint by first-class mail, postage prepaid

claims.claim: The mailing is to the person to be served at the place where the papers were left.
claims.quote: to the person to be served at the place where a copy of the summons and complaint were left.

claims.claim: Service is complete on the 10th day after mailing.
claims.quote: Service of a summons in this manner is deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing.

claims.claim: In the ordinary civil action described, the summons must direct the defendant to file a written response with the court.
claims.quote: A direction that the defendant file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint
claims.note: This is a claim about the direction in the summons.

claims.claim: The stated response period is 30 days after the summons is served on the defendant.
claims.quote: within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.

claims.claim: Exclude the first day when counting.
claims.quote: excluding the first day

claims.claim: Include the last day unless it is a holiday, in which case it is excluded.
claims.quote: including the last, unless the last day is a holiday, and then it is also excluded.

claims.claim: The replacement Section 415.20 becomes operative January 1, 2027.
claims.quote: This section shall become operative on January 1, 2027.

claims.claim: Under the replacement subdivision, good-faith attempts at personal delivery show reasonable diligence when the specified attempt requirements are met.
claims.quote: For purposes of this subdivision, a party shows reasonable diligence by attempting personal delivery of the summons and complaint, in good faith, on at least three occasions on three different days at three different times.

claims.claim: There must be at least three attempts.
claims.quote: on at least three occasions

claims.claim: The attempts must occur on three different days.
claims.quote: on three different days

claims.claim: The attempts must occur at three different times.
claims.quote: at three different times.

claims.claim: In a consumer-debt collection action, at least one attempt must be at the person's home or usual place of abode if that location is known or reasonably ascertainable.
claims.quote: In an action to collect “consumer debt,” as defined in Section 1788.2 of the Civil Code, at least one of the service attempts shall be made at the dwelling place or usual place of abode of the person to be served, provided that the dwelling place or usual place of abode is known or could be determined with reasonable effort.

claims.claim: USPS first-class mail remains an option in 2027.
claims.quote: by United States Postal Service first-class mail

claims.claim: Priority Mail with tracking is a 2027 option.
claims.quote: Priority Mail with tracking

claims.claim: Certified Mail with return receipt requested is a 2027 option.
claims.quote: Certified Mail with return receipt requested, with postage prepaid

claims.claim: Under the replacement version, service is still complete on the 10th day after mailing.
claims.quote: Service of a summons in this manner is deemed complete on the 10th day after the mailing.

flags.text: January 1, 2027 changes the diligence standard and mailing options, not the date service is deemed complete. The draft distinguishes the two versions.

result.summary: The claims are supported within the stated subdivision (b) scope. Both versions measure completion from mailing, not from the day the papers are left. The 30-day response period runs from service.
